governance.note: Builds on the pjm-48 coal keeper + pjm-49 seam-price corrections. Three new seam levers, each tracing to a measured/documented input and never to the realized net-interchange target (rule #11): (1) FIRM SCHEDULED-EXPORT FLOOR (firm_export_floor_by_year) = the p10 of PJM's OWN published per-tie SCHEDULED interchange (Data Miner import_export_act_sch_interchange sched_flow), i.e. the export reliably scheduled in >=90% of hours -- the firm contractual base, NOT the realized actual_flow that is scored. Its forward analogue is the contracted firm capacity/energy schedule (rule #12); forecast years carry no floor (byte-identical). (2) HURDLE 2.0->1.0: a physical decomposition, not a flow fit -- the firm transmission-service component of the old OMS-RSC $2 is paid by the firm scheduled flow (now the floor), leaving marginal delivery losses (~3% x ~$35/MWh ~= $1) as the only friction on the incremental economic flow (under the PJM-MISO/PJM-NYISO JOAs the coordinated economic flow pays no pancaked wheeling). (3) TVA + LGEE import seams priced on the documented ~$30/MWh SERC-bilateral basis (HR 11.6, identical to the reconciled Carolinas), limits 1600/1100 MW from the p99.5 of PJM's measured per-tie flow; PJM's own per-tie data VALIDATES the net-import direction, it does not set it. No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a price or volume residual; no unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals. Outage source is the exogenous CAMPD unit-level net-load-filtered windows (unchanged from the keeper).
governance.measured_source_gap_2025: DOCUMENTED MEASURED-SOURCE LIMITATION (not a model miss): in 2025 the EIA-930 PJM net-interchange total (+18.0 TWh) sits ~15 TWh BELOW PJM's OWN per-tie scheduled/actual sum (+32.9 TWh); 2023 and 2024 the two measured sources agree (~+40 / ~+33). No seam model can close a gap between two measured sources. 2025 is therefore scored against BOTH targets and flagged: against the per-tie sum the seam reproduces the total well; against EIA-930 it reads high purely from this inter-source basis gap. A second-order contributor on the EIA-930 side is the NYISO seam still pricing off NYISO's NYC-weighted SYSTEM-average LMP rather than the PJM-NY (west-NY) border (the scope-B border-price re-anchor is a follow-up gated on a committed west-NY hourly LMP extract).
